The Worker Process

src/worker.js — a second, standalone Node process that's the only place the scan actually runs, started with its own npm run worker.

// Figure 6.6: the job processor BullMQ calls (src/jobs/slaScan.job.js)
import env from '../config/env.js';
import { escalateOverdueTickets } from '../services/ticket.service.js';

const processSlaScan = async () => {
  const escalatedCount = await escalateOverdueTickets(env.SLA_BREACH_HOURS);
  return { escalatedCount };
};

export default processSlaScan;

Deliberately thin — every actual decision (what "overdue" means, how to mark a ticket escalated, what event to emit) already happened in the previous topic's service function. This file's only job is the glue BullMQ needs: a plain function that takes a job and returns a result.

// Figure 6.7: the worker entry point (src/worker.js)
import './events/index.js';
import { Worker } from 'bullmq';
import connection from './config/redis.js';
import { QUEUE_NAME } from './jobs/slaScan.queue.js';
import processSlaScan from './jobs/slaScan.job.js';

const worker = new Worker(QUEUE_NAME, processSlaScan, { connection });

worker.on('completed', (job, result) => {
  console.log(`[worker] ${job.name} completed — escalated ${result.escalatedCount} ticket(s).`);
});

worker.on('failed', (job, err) => {
  console.error(`[worker] ${job?.name ?? 'job'} failed:`, err);
});

This is a whole separate file run as its own process — npm run worker, never imported by app.js or server.js — and it's the reason for that import './events/index.js' at the top. That import is a side effect (see Week 5): it registers every domain-event listener by module-loading each one. server.js already does this via app.js, but registering a listener only affects the process that ran the .on() call — an EventEmitter's listeners live in that process's memory, not in Redis or anywhere shared. Without its own copy of this import, the worker process would call domainEvents.emit(EVENTS.TICKET_SLA_BREACHED, ticket) in escalateOverdueTickets and nothing would happen — no listener in this process to hear it. What each of those three listeners actually manages to do once they are registered here is the next topic.
